paper_title: Search for oscillations of fundamental constants using molecular spectroscopy
suggested_experiment_name: I2 molecular spectroscopy UDM search (Expt A: Nd:YAG/532nm; Expt B: Ti:Sapphire/725nm)
coupling_convention: Q_hat_N . d_vec, the dimensionless linear combination of scalar UDM couplings to the QCD sector (0.999 d_gs + 0.092 d_mhat + 3e-4 d_deltam + 0.047 d_ms), exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 3
notes: Oswald et al. (arXiv:2111.06883): first direct bounds on oscillating UDM coupling to gluons/quarks (nuclear-mass variation) via I2 molecular spectroscopy, 10 Hz - 100 MHz (m_phi ~ 4e-14 to 4e-7 eV). Primary new result is Fig. 3 exclusion on Q_N_hat.d (QCD-sector combination, dominated by gluon coupling d_gs), best mapped to ScalarNucleon since it constrains nucleon-mass variation. No numerical table is provided; data_points are reconstructed from the reported fractional frequency sensitivities (delta_nu/nu ~ 1e-15 to 5e-14 for Expt A, ~6e-15 for Expt B), sensitivities Delta_R_N ~ 0.06-0.07, phi0/M_Pl = sqrt(2*rho)/(m_phi*M_Pl) with rho = 0.3 GeV/cm^3, and the stochastic factor-3 penalty; values are order-of-magnitude estimates consistent with the Fig. 3 axis range (1e-3 to 1e9+). Paper also gives new bounds on d_alpha (ScalarPhoton) and d_me (ScalarElectron) in Figs. 4a/4b; only the novel QCD-sector limit is extracted here. Solar-halo and Earth-halo scenarios yield stronger bounds (higher assumed local density, e.g. 1e5 x 0.3 GeV/cm^3 for solar halo) but the galactic halo (0.3 GeV/cm^3) is the standard scenario encoded. Earth/solar halo scenarios assume overdense bound halos, not the standard rho=0.4 GeV/cm^3.
